subject: Request: Conditional downsell safety-net + ramp opt-out — exec sign-off needed
messages:
From: Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.com>
To: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-11-12T09:15:00-08:00
Subject: BluePeak — request for downsell safety net and midterm opt-out language

Vanessa / Karthik — forwarding BluePeak thread (attached SOW_v2). Quick context: BluePeak is a 3-region healthcare platform evaluating a 12‑month committed plan with a phasing ramp (months 1–3 onboarding high-touch, months 4–12 steady state). They are asking for two nonstandard asks to get the signed PO this week: 

1) A "downsell safety net": if they need to drop from committed 5M credits to no less than 3M within month 4–9, we offer a one-time credit buffer (prorated) and lock a step-down price floor rather than immediate full early-termination charges.
2) An opt-out clause for months 4–6 if a defined performance metric (p99 latency across three regions) is not met for two consecutive weeks — they want it to be bilateral.

Neha's ask: can Deal Desk/Exec approve a conditional addendum that: (a) limits the safety net to a single downshift in term once, (b) caps total finance exposure at 20% of committed ARR in year 1, (c) requires a 30‑day notice plus a 45‑day ramp down schedule, and (d) makes the opt-out unilateral only after a remediation window (we'd prefer remediation then right to cure).

Attached: SOW_v2.pdf (redlined) and an initial addendum draft (Redwood-Offramp-Addendum.docx).

Neha
Account Executive — Redwood Inference
neha_kapoor@redwood.com
+1 415-555-0192

---
From: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.com>
To: Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-11-12T11:02:00-08:00
Subject: Re: BluePeak — request for downsell safety net and midterm opt-out language

Thanks Neha — looping Karthik for deal‑desk guidance. My quick read: I support a constrained safety net if we (1) keep it one-time only, (2) insist on the price floor, and (3) build in strict telemetry requirements so we don't inadvertently under-index. For the opt-out, we should require a 14‑day remediation period and a 30‑day notice window before any unilateral opt-out.

Karthik — can you draft recommended language we can share with BluePeak tomorrow? If this needs exec sign-off (more than a 15% credit concession), I can run to Marissa. We need to be specific about exposure cap and the billing mechanics (how credits are calculated and applied).

V.
Vanessa Ortiz
Strategic Sales — Redwood Inference
vanessa_ortiz@redwood.com

---
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
To: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.com>, Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-11-12T14:45:00-08:00
Subject: Re: BluePeak — draft addendum language and exposure calc

Vanessa / Neha — drafted key points below (see attached Redwood-Offramp-Addendum.docx for full redline):

- One-time downsell safety net: Customer may exercise a single reduction in committed credits during months 4–9. Reduction is prorated over remaining term and capped to a single step-down.
- Finance exposure cap: Company liability capped at 20% of year‑1 committed ARR; any residual shortfall reverts to standard termination charges.
- Ramp-down schedule: 30‑day notice + staged reduction over 45 days (15/30 split) to avoid headroom cliffs.
- Price floor: A guaranteed per‑unit floor for any step-down period (no lower than 80% of committed unit price).
- Opt-out for performance: Customer may notify after two consecutive weeks of p99 region latency > threshold, but Redwood has 14 days to remediate and must provide an agreed mitigation plan. Only after failed remediation can customer elect a 30‑day termination window.

Ask: we believe these terms are reasonable and keep financial exposure contained. However, the 20% cap with the one-time concession equates to an estimated $420k potential credit here — this crosses the standard approval threshold. Requesting Marissa's exec sign-off (or approval of an alternate cap).

Karthik
Sr. Deal Desk Manager — Redwood Inference
karthik_iyer@redwood.com

---
From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
To: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>, Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-11-13T09:08:00-08:00
Subject: RE: BluePeak — draft addendum language and exposure calc

Team — reviewed the draft and the exposure numbers. I appreciate the conservative guardrails. Approveable under the following executive conditions: 

1) Limit the safety net to a single calendar quarter step-down (not arbitrary month window) between month 4–9.
2) Reduce company exposure cap to 15% of year‑1 committed ARR (from 20%), but allow Deal Desk to escalate to CFO approval for a higher cap if there is documented strategic value (customer reference, enterprise roadmap alignment).
3) Add a clause that credits are applied as bill credits over the next two billing cycles; no cash refunds.
4) Ensure the remediation plan template is attached to the addendum and we own the remediation timeline and reporting cadence.

Marissa will sign off once Karthik updates the addendum with the 15% cap language and the quarter-step constraint. BluePeak should get a clean redline and a short cover note explaining the changes.

-Marissa
VP, Revenue Operations — Redwood Inference
marissa_cole@redwood.com

---
From: Ava Green <ava.green@bluepeakhealth.com>
To: Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.com>, Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.com>
Cc: Procurement <procurement@bluepeakhealth.com>
Date: 2026-11-13T13:22:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Redwood addendum draft — BluePeak feedback

Thanks for the quick turnaround and transparency. A few clarifying questions before we sign: 

- We appreciate the one-time limitation, but can the step-down window be tied to "first full quarter following an approved request" rather than "single calendar quarter"? That gives us predictable billing alignment.
- The 15% cap is acceptable as a starting point; however, Procurement requests the right to request CFO-level review before execution.
- For the remediation plan: will Redwood commit to weekly telemetry reports during the remediation window? We need the operational signal to decide whether to proceed with step-down.

We can sign when the addendum reflects weekly telemetry and clarifies the quarter-def timing language to protect billing alignment.

Best,
Ava Green
Head of Platform Engineering — BluePeak Health
ava.green@bluepeakhealth.com

---
From: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.com>
To: Ava Green <ava.green@bluepeakhealth.com>, Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-11-14T17:03:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Redwood addendum draft — BluePeak feedback (Exec approval confirmed)

Ava — thanks for the clear requests. Per Marissa's sign-off and the updated addendum (attached), we can accept the "first full quarter following an approved request" language to align billing. We have updated the liability cap to 15% of year‑1 committed ARR, with an explicit path for Procurement to request CFO review prior to execution. Weekly telemetry will be provided during any remediation window; Redwood will own the remediation plan and the reporting cadence. Credits will be applied as bill credits across two billing cycles.

Karthik has updated the redline and I attached the clean addendum and an executive cover note to this thread. Marissa has authorized signature pending the final DocuSign routing. We will not open additional concessions beyond what's in the addendum; exercise still counts as the single allowed downsell event.

If you confirm, we'll send DocuSign this afternoon and target a start date the first day of next quarter for the committed term.

Thanks — looking forward to getting this done.

Vanessa Ortiz
Strategic Sales — Redwood Inference
vanessa_ortiz@redwood.com

Attachments: Redwood-Offramp-Addendum.docx (redline and clean), SOW_v2.pdf
